item.title: Jewish charity ambulance attack investigated by counter terrorism police
item.description: Counter terrorism police are leading the investigation into a suspected antisemitic hate crime in North London, after four ambulances belonging to a Jewish volunteer group were set on fire, in a synagogue car park. Nearby homes had to be evacuated as a precaution.

item.title: Labour government reveals plans for seven new towns in England
item.description: The government has revealed the location of seven potential new towns across England, each delivering between 10,000 and 40,000 new homes.

item.title: Israeli tanks mass on Lebanon’s border increasing invasion fears
item.description: In Lebanon, there have been further Israeli airstrikes, including one targeting another bridge in the south of the country, which is becoming increasingly cut off from the rest of Lebanon.

item.title: Israel must ‘achieve key objectives’ before Iran ceasefire – Naftali Bennett
item.description: We spoke to former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett.

item.title: How UK has become a country music hotspot
item.description: Once the soundtrack to rural, small-town America, country music is now having its UK moment thanks to streaming platforms putting the genre in front of a new generation, writes Minnie Stephenson.

item.title: Are some of Britain’s vape shops a front to groom schoolchildren?
item.description: There are calls for strict new checks on vape sellers after a police warning that vape shops and mini marts are being used as fronts to groom schoolchildren.

item.title: We can’t turn away again, says grooming gang whistleblower
item.description: We spoke to Maggie Oliver, the former detective constable with Greater Manchester Police who blew the whistle on the Rochdale grooming scandal.

item.title: Trump hits out at Europe over Strait of Hormuz
item.description: The rift between Donald Trump and his European allies seems to grow wider by the day.

item.title: King Charles US visit to go ahead in April
item.description: Despite President Trump's latest outburst, Buckingham Palace has announced that King Charles will go ahead with his state visit to the US late next month, to celebrate 250 years since America rose up against our monarchy.

item.title: There is an emerging new world order of predators – Historian Peter Frankopan
item.description: We spoke to Peter Frankopan, a Professor of Global History at Oxford University, and asked him if this rupture between President Trump and his European allies is a new low.

item.title: Israel passes death penalty law for Palestinians convicted of fatal attacks
item.description: Israel says it will destroy all the homes along Lebanon's border with Israel and stop 600,000 residents who fled southern Lebanon from returning to their villages.

item.title: ‘Barbaric’ death penalty law is ‘despicable’, says Israeli human rights lawyer
item.description: We spoke to Michael Svard, who's an Israeli human rights lawyer, and asked him why Israel has approved this law, given that it hasn't executed anyone since 1962.

item.title: Scott Mills questioned in 2018 over allegations of serious sexual assault against boy aged under 16
item.description: Police say sacked Radio 2 DJ Scott Mills was questioned in 2018 over allegations of serious sexual offences against a boy aged under 16.

item.title: Artemis II: NASA’s first manned mission around the moon in 50 years
item.description: Mankind is due to embark on its first mission to the moon since 1972. But unlike Apollo, the Artemis 2 crew includes the first female, Black and non-American astronauts to fly a moon mission.

item.title: Israel’s controversial new death penalty law explained… the breakdown
item.description: Israel has passed a law permitting the death penalty as punishment for those convicted of deadly terrorism. Far-right politicians in the Knesset - the Israeli parliament - succeeded in passing the law, which they say is needed to stop Palestinians from carrying out deadly attacks or kidnapping Israelis to use in swap deals.
